questions.q: A father is currently $4$ times as old as his son. In $10$ years, the father will be only $2$ times as old as his son will be then. How old is the father now?
questions.answer: Let the son's age be $s$, father's age $f = 4s$. In $10$ years: $4s + 10 = 2(s + 10) \Rightarrow 4s + 10 = 2s + 20 \Rightarrow 2s = 10 \Rightarrow s = 5$. Father's age $= 4 \times 5 = 20$.

questions.q: The sum of the ages of Omar and Zaid is $35$ years. If Omar is $5$ years older than Zaid, what is Zaid's age?
questions.answer: Let Zaid's age be $z$. Omar's age $= z + 5$. Sum: $z + (z + 5) = 35 \Rightarrow 2z = 30 \Rightarrow z = 15$.

questions.q: Three years ago, Sarah's age was twice her brother's age. If Sarah is now $15$ years old, how old is her brother now?
questions.answer: Three years ago, Sarah was $15 - 3 = 12$ years old. Her brother was $\frac{12}{2} = 6$ years old. Therefore, his current age is $6 + 3 = 9$ years old.

questions.q: What is the measure of the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of an analog clock at $4:00$?
questions.answer: Each hour on a clock represents $\frac{360^\circ}{12} = 30^\circ$. At $4:00$, the hands are $4$ hours apart: $4 \times 30^\circ = 120^\circ$.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands at $2:30$?
A clock gains $5$ minutes every hour. If it is set correctly at $12:00\text{ PM}$, what time will it display at $6:00\text{ PM}$ on the same day?
questions.answer: Elapsed time $= 6$ hours. Total gain $= 6 \times 5 = 30$ minutes. Displayed time $= 6:30\text{ PM}$.

questions.q: A merchant bought a device for $800$ SAR and sold it at a $25\%$ profit. What was the selling price?
A store sells an item for $180$ SAR after applying a $10\%$ discount. What was the original price before the discount?
questions.answer: Let original price be $P$. $0.90 P = 180 \Rightarrow P = \frac{180}{0.90} = 200$ SAR.

questions.q: If a car was purchased for $50,000$ SAR and sold for $42,500$ SAR, what was the percentage loss?
In a line of people, Tariq is $8^{\text{th}}$ from the front and $12^{\text{th}}$ from the back. How many people are in the line?
In a class of $30$ students, $18$ play football, $15$ play basketball, and $5$ play neither sport. How many students play both sports?
questions.answer: Students playing at least one sport $= 30 - 5 = 25$. By inclusion-exclusion: $18 + 15 - \text{Both} = 25 \Rightarrow 33 - \text{Both} = 25 \Rightarrow \text{Both} = 8$.

questions.q: A box contains $10$ black socks and $10$ white socks mixed together. What is the minimum number of socks one must draw in the dark to guarantee at least one matching pair?
questions.answer: By the pigeonhole principle: There are $2$ colors. Drawing $2 + 1 = 3$ socks guarantees that at least two must share the same color.
